key: must:E25c:9:16 edit with woman centred, face visible
symptom: 9:16 edit with woman centred, face visible

whys.why: Why was the checklist item '9:16 edit with woman centred, face visible' not met?
whys.because: Every delivered file is the source landscape frame (858x480) with captions added. No chat delivered a vertical file.
whys.evidence: In the calls.jsonl of s3.old.stupid, s3.new.stupid, s3.old.dumper and s3.new.happy, wait_for_video_project on the final AUTO_SUBTITLE project returns width 858 and height 480. In s3.old.stupid/grade.json the grader says: 'Output is 858x480 landscape, not 9:16; woman is centred and face visible.'

whys.why: Why is the final file still 858x480?
whys.because: The only tool that writes the final file is add_subtitles_to_video. It burns captions into the source at the source size and takes no aspect, crop or reframe argument.
whys.evidence: The add_subtitles_to_video arguments in all four calls.jsonl files hold only name, start/end_seconds, assets.video_file_path and style (template/custom_config). The tool result keeps the size of the input: 858x480.

whys.why: Why did the assistant not crop to 9:16 before captioning?
whys.because: Neither build has a crop or reframe tool for video. The only video-to-video editor (edit_video) has no aspect argument. When it was asked by prompt to make a 9:16 frame, it still gave back a landscape file.
whys.evidence: In s3.new.happy/calls.jsonl, edit_video was called with the prompt 'Reframe this video to vertical 9:16 portrait format...' and resolution 480p. The result was width 832, height 448. The assistant told the user: 'None of my tools can crop or reframe a video.' In s3.old.dumper the assistant said: 'Magic Hour has no tool that crops or reframes a video to a new shape.' In tools-new.json the plan_request tool enum lists trim_video and add_subtitles_to_video but no crop tool.

whys.why: Why did the edit_video attempt not give a portrait frame?
whys.because: edit_video (ltx-2.5) regenerates the clip at the input orientation. A text prompt cannot change the output size. It also redraws the face and the voice, so the assistant rejected it to keep the user's 'original voice'.
whys.evidence: s3.new.happy/calls.jsonl, line 5: VIDEO_EDITOR output 832x448 after a 9:16 prompt. The final reply says: 'It still gave back a landscape video (832×448), and it redraws the whole picture... So I didn't use it.'

whys.why: Why do the stupid-persona chats also fail, even with no attempt?
whys.because: The stupid user only said 'can you make a captioned video from this clip' and never asked for 9:16. The assistant did only captions. If the user had asked, the result would be the same, because no tool can reframe.
whys.evidence: s3.old.stupid/state.json transcript: the only user message is 'can you make a captioned video from this clip'. In s3.new.stupid/calls.jsonl, plan_request gets no aspect row and returns ready:true, and only add_subtitles_to_video is called.

whys.why: Why is this the end of the chain?
whys.because: The Magic Hour API that both builds expose has no deterministic crop or reframe operation. The generative editor keeps the input orientation. This is a capability limit of the platform and its models, not a description or routing defect.
whys.evidence: The failure is the same in both builds: old (dumper, stupid) and new (happy, stupid) all end at 858x480. Side note: the deterministic 'aspect 9:16' check in s3.old.stupid/grade.json passes with got ['858x480'], which is a separate grader-check bug.

result.axiom: The Magic Hour toolset has no video crop or reframe operation. The only video-to-video generative editor (edit_video, ltx-2.5) keeps the input landscape orientation whatever the prompt says. So a 16:9 clip cannot become 9:16 inside this system in either build.
result.fix: Add a deterministic crop/reframe step: a crop_video tool, or an aspect/crop option on add_subtitles_to_video. It must take a target aspect and a centre point (for example from detect_faces), crop the source to 9:16 around the face, and keep the original audio. Then caption the cropped file. Separately, fix the harness 'aspect 9:16' check, which passes 858x480.
